izzyondroid:com.clearevo.bluetooth_gnss.summary: Connect your phone to external Bluetooth GPS/GLONASS/Galileo/BeiDou receivers
izzyondroid:com.clearevo.bluetooth_gnss.description:
Bluetooth GNSS lets you use accurate satellite positioning from powerful external Bluetooth GPS/Galileo/GLONASS/BeiDou receivers instead of the less powerful internal A-GPS of phones/tablets - for better location accuracy with your favorite Maps and Navigation apps like Google Maps, etc.
 You must first get an external Bluetooth GNSS/GPS device like the EcoDroidGPS (www.ClearEvo.com), HOLUX, Garmin GLO, etc to use with this app, which is free and open-source software. If your Bluetooth GNSS/GPS device supports RTK, this app also supports overlay of NTRIP server data streams for professional RTK positioning (centimeter-level accuracy - depends on device).
 This app supports showing ’Accuracy’ estimates from the U-Blox ’PUBX’ accuracy messages, instead of the commonly used ’HDOP x CEP’ method. This PUBX accuracy reading exactly matches as is the same source of the ’Accuracy’ as shown in U-Center PC tool when connected directly to the M8030 (EcoDroidGPS) or ZED-F9P (EcoDroidGPS + ArduSimple) devices via USB.
 How to test if your target app uses the mock location from this app or not: during a connection, create a file named ’bt_gnss_test_debug_mock_location_1_1_mode_flag’ in internal storage (adb command: touch /sdcard/bt_gnss_test_debug_mock_location_1_1_mode_flag ) and see if your target app now shows lat as 1.0 and lon as 1.0 or not, remove/delete the file to resume using real lat lon from connected bluetooth device.

izzyondroid:com.keshav.capturesposed.name: CaptureSposed
izzyondroid:com.keshav.capturesposed.summary: Block Android's Screenshot and Screen Recording Detection APIs
izzyondroid:com.keshav.capturesposed.description:
With the release of Android 14, Google added an API to enable app developers to detect screenshots. This API has since been adopted by popular apps such as Snapchat.
 CaptureSposed is an Xposed module that effectively disables this API as well as the screen recording detection API added in Android 15. The app provides in-app switches to control each hook. You can also add optional Quick Settings tiles that mirror the in-app switches.
 ⚠️ WARNING: CaptureSposed is intended for rooted devices running Android 14 or newer and requires Xposed. The required Xposed variant to use is LSPosed. Other Xposed variants will not work. This module cannot be guaranteed to work on all devices. In the worst case, it can cause a bootloop. Use at your own risk. Additionally, this module does not protect against screenshot detection from apps that use the pre-Android 14 approach of using file system listeners to detect screenshots ( ref 1 , ref 2 ).
 To use CaptureSposed:
 Install an LSPosed build with API 101 support. This requires your device to be rooted with Magisk or KernelSU.
 Install CaptureSposed.
 Grant root access to CaptureSposed.
 Activate the CaptureSposed module in the LSposed user interface.
 Reboot your device and sign in.
 Open the CaptureSposed app and use the switches to enable or disable screenshot and screen recording detection blocking. Use the Testing card to verify that detection is blocked when expected.
 Optionally, add the Block Screenshot Detection and Block Recording Detection Quick Settings tiles from the tile editor. These tiles mirror the in-app switches.
 CaptureSposed is a collaborative project by Keshav Majeti and David Berdik.

fdroid:app.quorumpony.name: QuorumPony
fdroid:app.quorumpony.summary: Split a secret into printable cards. Any K of N recover it. Fully offline.
fdroid:app.quorumpony.description:
QuorumPony splits a secret — an age or GPG key, a seed phrase, a password — into N shares using Shamir's Secret Sharing over GF(2^8). Any K shares reconstruct the secret; any K−1 reveal nothing about it.
Each share becomes a printable card with a QR code and a hand-typeable code (Crockford base32, so 0/O and 1/I/L can't be confused). Export all cards as a PDF, print them, and hand them to people or places you trust.
Features:
• Split a secret from text or a file into 2–16 cards with a chosen threshold
• Recover by scanning QR codes with the camera, or typing codes by hand
• Check cards: verify a card is intact and part of a backup, without reconstructing the secret
• Two-layer integrity: a per-card checksum catches damaged or mistyped cards instantly; an envelope hash confirms the recovered secret is exactly what was backed up
• Printable PDF of all cards
• Optional biometric/device-credential lock
• Six languages: English, Español, Deutsch, Français, 日本語, Português (Brasil)
Fully offline: no network permission, no analytics, no accounts. The cryptographic core is open source and pinned byte-for-byte to cross-implementation test vectors shared with the iOS app and a Python reference implementation.

fdroid:barilyuk.mobilosignal.name: MobiloSignal
fdroid:barilyuk.mobilosignal.summary: Find the best spot for calls and mobile internet by seeing signal strength
fdroid:barilyuk.mobilosignal.description:
Mobilosignal shows your Android phone’s real-time cellular signal strength in dBm. The value is always visible in the status bar and in a notification, even while you use other apps.
Unlike signal bars, dBm is a precise measurement of radio signal power, allowing you to see actual network conditions instead of a simplified guess.
Practical uses of monitoring signal strength in dBm:
 📞 Prevent call drops in weak areas
 If signal falls below about -105 dBm, voice calls become unstable even if bars are still visible. Seeing this in advance lets you move a few steps before dialing instead of losing the call mid-conversation.
 🎮 Avoid lag spikes during mobile gaming
 Online games become unstable below roughly -95 dBm. Monitoring this lets you reposition before starting a match instead of dealing with unpredictable lag or disconnects.
 🎥 Stable video uploads and streaming
 Upload-heavy tasks such as live streaming or sending large videos require stronger signal, typically better than -90 dBm. dBm lets you confirm the connection is sufficient before starting.
 🚗 Predict signal loss on daily routes
 While commuting, you will notice exact dBm values where signal consistently drops below usable levels. This allows planning calls or downloads outside those zones instead of discovering the problem every day.
 🏠 Choose the exact spot for hotspot usage
 When using your phone as a hotspot, performance depends directly on signal strength. Moving from -105 dBm to -85 dBm can multiply speed several times. The app shows exactly where that improvement happens.
 🔋 Explain sudden battery drain
 If your phone sits at -110 dBm for long periods, it continuously boosts transmission power. This is a measurable cause of fast battery drain, not some mysterious background app.
 🏢 Find the one place in a building that works
 In offices, basements, or elevators, signal can change from -75 dBm to -115 dBm within a few meters. The app helps you locate the one usable spot instead of guessing or walking randomly.
 📡 Verify signal improvement objectively exists
 After installing a repeater or moving near a window, you can confirm improvement numerically, for example from -108 dBm to -82 dBm, instead of relying on subjective “feels better”.
 📶 Decide when to switch to Wi-Fi
 If cellular drops below about -100 dBm while Wi-Fi is available, switching avoids slow speeds and packet loss. The decision becomes data-driven instead of reactive.
 🔄 Compare network conditions across time
 Observe how signal varies during the day. Consistent drops at specific hours indicate tower congestion or load issues rather than physical coverage problems.
 ⚠ Identify false “full bars” situations
 Some phones display high bars even at -95 dBm or worse. Seeing the real value prevents trusting misleading UI and explains why performance does not match what the screen suggests.
 📶 Detect unstable signal before drops happen
 Signal bars on Android are not standardized and are defined by device manufacturers and carrier configuration. As a result, visually “strong” signal may still correspond to borderline radio conditions (around -95 to -105 dBm). dBm reveals radio signal degradation in real time, allowing you to react before calls drop or data stalls.
 ⚠ Separate signal problems from network problems
 Strong signal (e.g. -70 dBm) with poor internet performance indicates carrier-side congestion. Weak signal (e.g. below -105 dBm) indicates coverage limitations. This distinction prevents incorrect troubleshooting.
Mobilosignal turns your Android phone into a precise signal indicating tool, replacing unreliable signal bars with quantitative data about connectivity and network troubleshooting.
Created by Eugen Barilyuk EB43 https://eb43.github.io

fdroid:com.quaap.audiometer.name: AudioMeter
fdroid:com.quaap.audiometer.description:
A simple VU-style audio meter. You can choose from several formulas to allow
the meter to work in low- and high-noise level enviromnents.
I noticed there was no audio meter in F-Droid, so I thought I'd build one.
The app offers a few ways to calculate the audio level to display:
* dBFS: Decibels relative to Full Scale.
* RMS: Root Mean Square. This is arguable the most correct, but it is a little insensitive at low volumes.
* LogRMS: Natural log of RMS: My first attempt to even out the scale. It's a little too sensitive to noisy mics.
* SqrtRMS: Squareroot of RMS: My second attempt to even out RMS: it seems to works best.
* Max: Simply find the loudest bit of each sample. Most responsive, but will peg the scale on noisey places.
* Avg: Simple average of the sound.

fdroid:com.tyraen.voicekeyboard.summary: Speech-to-text keyboard that uses your own Whisper API key
fdroid:com.tyraen.voicekeyboard.description:
Voice Keyboard is a keyboard that types what you say. Switch to it in any text field, tap the microphone, speak, and the text lands in whatever app you are using.
Speech recognition needs an API key for a supported service, such as Groq or Mistral, or a server of your own. Audio goes only to your configured endpoint. Compatible Chat Completions services also work; the model must accept your device's recording format.
 Voice input

 Works in any text field, in any app
 Processing queue: start the next recording while the previous one is still being transcribed
 Cancel only the latest unfinished dictation during recording, recognition, post-processing or retry; earlier recordings continue
 Optional voice input for other apps through Android speech recognition or a dictation window. Off by default, uses your saved provider, without post-processing or context
 Offline-proof keyboard dictation: a recording that cannot be sent is kept on the device and resent automatically once the connection returns
 Several dictation languages on one key: tap to cycle, long-press to pick from the list
 Custom vocabulary for names and technical terms that get misrecognised
 Can be the voice input of another keyboard, such as HeliBoard, and hand back to it once the text is typed
 Optional post-processing 
 Fix punctuation, spelling and filler words
 Shorten, add emoji, rewrite as verse, or translate
 Optional recent dictation context helps recover misheard names and terms. Off by default; remembers up to 5 of your own recent dictations only in memory and sends them to the selected provider as reference. Context is shared across chats in the same app and clears when input moves to another app. It does not read conversations.
 Terminal mode turns dictation into shell commands
 Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible provider such as OpenRouter; editing prompts are customizable
 Optional correction tools · Beta

 Basic letter keyboard for quick corrections: 14 layouts, including French, German, Russian, Hindi and Arabic, with accents and symbols; no predictions, swipe typing or CJK conversion
 Actions on selected text: proofread, translate or give a one-time instruction using your configured post-processing provider. Review before Apply; Undo is available while the inserted text stays selected and unchanged
 Keyboard 
 One tap takes you back to the keyboard you came from
 Saved texts keep dictations that finish after leaving their original field. Insert, copy or delete them individually; background results do not replace your clipboard
 Optional compact Terminal panel with full-size controls and instant expansion; off by default
 Punctuation keys, accelerating backspace, send key, persistent clipboard bar
 The Enter key runs the field's own action: Search, Go, Send, Next or Done
 The microphone is off in password fields
 Spacing around dictated text follows the text already in the field
 Light, dark and automatic themes; 17 interface languages
 Privacy 
 No analytics, no advertising, no tracking, no account, no servers of our own

* Classic grid-based territory capture — step, draw, and close the loop to claim ground.

* A folded-ribbon trail, smooth "virus" death dissolves, and a live minimap.
* Light and dark themes, and a random player colour each game.
* A local high score. No accounts, no ads, no tracking, no network access.
* Tiny download and fully playable offline.

Gaidly is a trip planner for people who want to turn a travel idea into a plan they can actually use. Pick a destination, say how long you have, add your preferences and let Gaidly build a travel itinerary around the kind of trip you want to take.
Start with the basics. Tell Gaidly where you are going, how many days you have and what you want from the trip. You might care about food, museums, beaches, slower days, busy days, places that work for a group, or constraints that need to shape the plan. Gaidly uses that context to organise a trip rather than giving you a random list of travel ideas.
The result is useful when you have a destination but do not know where to go first, and when you only have a rough idea of the kind of break you want. Planning a weekend trip? Put the time you have at the centre of the plan. Thinking about a solo trip or a road trip? Start with the places and the pace that suit you. Looking for things to do on a holiday? Use your interests to create a clearer starting point.
Gaidly can also help with trips that involve more than one stop. Plan a journey across multiple cities or countries and keep the itinerary tied to the time you actually have. A useful trip plan is not a race to squeeze every landmark into a day. It helps you decide what fits, what can wait and which places belong together.
Use Gaidly to:
• plan a trip before you lock in the rest of the travel details;
• create a personalised itinerary around your destination, dates and preferences;
• organise a solo trip, a road trip, a weekend away or a longer vacation;
• find places, attractions and things to do that make sense for the trip you are planning;
• bring several travel ideas into one plan instead of keeping them scattered across tabs;
• use a pasted travel-post URL as a starting point for a new itinerary.
You do not need to search every place separately and hope the pieces work together. Gaidly gives you a more organised way to make choices before the trip begins. Use the itinerary as a guide, change direction when your plans change and leave room for the parts of travel that should stay spontaneous.
Before you settle the details, use the plan to compare possibilities at a sensible pace. Think about how much time each idea needs, which places suit the rhythm of the trip and whether it makes more sense to stay in one area or split the days between stops. That is useful when people in the same group want different things. The trip can start with the conversation, rather than with a fixed list that nobody chose.

apple-macos:6800385386.name: Book of Enoch: Audio & Study
apple-macos:6800385386.description:
NEW IN THE APP: JUBILEES AND JASHER
The Book of Jubilees (R. H. Charles) and Sefer HaYashar, the Book of Jasher (a medieval Hebrew midrash, Browne translation), each in English and Hebrew, with English audio.
The Book of Enoch (1 Enoch) is one of the great surviving works of ancient Jewish literature from the Second Temple period. Attributed to Enoch son of Jared, the man of Genesis 5 who walked with God, it tells of the Watchers, the fallen angels whose children were the Nephilim, of the judgment set for them, of the courses of the sun and the moon, and of visions that run to the end of days. This app gives you the complete book, all 108 chapters, with the Ge'ez text and five translations, to read, to listen to, and to study at your own pace.
THE COMPLETE BOOK, ALL FIVE PARTS
- The Book of the Watchers, chapters 1 to 36
- The Book of Parables, 37 to 71
- The Book of the Luminaries, 72 to 82
- The Book of Dream Visions, 83 to 90
- The Epistle of Enoch, 91 to 108
Every chapter is numbered verse by verse, so you can find and cite any passage.
READ THE GE'EZ TEXT ITSELF
The Book of Enoch survives complete only in Ge'ez, classical Ethiopic, and the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church holds it as part of the biblical canon. This app includes the Ge'ez text, chapter by chapter, so you can open the book as it has been read in Ethiopia for centuries and compare it with your translation.
FIVE TRANSLATIONS
- English, the R. H. Charles translation of 1917
- German, the Riessler translation of 1928
- Russian, the Smirnov translation of 1888
- French, the Martin translation of 1906
- Swedish, the translation of 1826
LISTEN TO THE BOOK OF ENOCH
Built-in audio reads the English text aloud, chapter after chapter, so you can listen while you drive, walk, or rest your eyes.
WORKS OFFLINE
The full text is stored on your device. Open the Book of Enoch on a plane, underground, or with no signal at all.
A PLAN THROUGH THE WHOLE BOOK
The built-in reading plan takes you through the book chapter by chapter, at your own pace, so you finish it instead of stopping after the Watchers.
ASK WHILE YOU READ
Rabbi AI is a study companion built into the app, in text or voice chat. Ask who the Watchers were, what the 364 day calendar is about, or how a passage relates to Genesis.
STUDY TOGETHER
A community chat inside the app lets you discuss what you are reading with other readers.
BUILT FOR STUDY
- Notes and highlights on any verse
- Bookmarks that take you back to where you stopped
- Day and night reading modes
- Verse numbers on, for citation and cross reference
FREE AND PREMIUM
Reading is free: the whole book, every translation and the Ge'ez text, the reading plan, and a daily allowance of audio and Rabbi AI questions. Premium removes the limits: unlimited Rabbi AI questions, voice chat, unlimited listening, and unlimited bookmarks.
WHAT THE BOOK OF ENOCH IS
1 Enoch is not part of the Hebrew Bible or of most Christian Old Testaments. It belongs to the apocrypha, the ancient Jewish writings that circulated widely in the Second Temple period. Aramaic fragments of it were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls at Qumran, it shaped how that generation thought about angels, judgment, and the calendar, and the complete text survived in the Ethiopian manuscript tradition. Whether you come to it as scripture, as history, or out of curiosity about the Watchers and the Nephilim, the app gives you the text itself, to read for yourself.
The app interface is available in English, German, Russian, French, and Swedish.

firefox-addons:3064463.name: Privacy for Bale Web
firefox-addons:3064463.summary: Blur chats, previews, media and avatars on Bale Web until you hover them. Everything stays on your device.Blur chats, previews, media and avatars on Bale Web until you hover them. Everything stays on your device.
firefox-addons:3064463.description:
Open Bale Web in an office, a cafe, a lecture hall or a screen share, and anyone
looking at your display can read your conversations. Privacy for Bale Web blurs the
private parts of the page and leaves the rest usable, so you can keep working without
turning your screen away from the room.
WHAT IT BLURS
Conversation names and message previews in the chat list
Message text, quoted replies, and link or document cards
Sender names in group conversations
Photos, video thumbnails, stickers and large emoji
Profile pictures - in the chat list, beside messages, in the conversation header and in
the profile panel
Optionally, the message you are currently typing
Each of these has its own switch, so you decide how much to hide. Timestamps, unread
counters and reply counts stay readable on purpose: they carry nothing private, and
they are what keeps a blurred screen usable.
HOW YOU READ SOMETHING
Move the pointer over a blurred element and just that element becomes readable. You can
add a short delay so passing the pointer across the screen does not flash your messages.
Hold Alt, Ctrl or Shift to reveal the whole screen while the key is down. Alt+Shift+B
turns blurring on and off in every open tab.
WHEN YOU WALK AWAY
Two optional settings re-blur everything the moment the window loses focus, or after a
period without keyboard or mouse activity. Both override the main switch, so stepping
away always hides the screen.
PRIVACY
The extension asks for one permission: saving your settings. It has no access to your
tabs or browsing history, it makes no network requests, it contains no analytics and no
remotely loaded code, and it never reads or transmits your messages. The blur is applied
visually to the page; the extension does not need to know what is on screen in order to
hide it.
It is free, open source under the MIT license, and the published packages are built from
the public source by an automated workflow.
Source code and issue tracker:
 https://github.com/amiranmanesh/bale-privacy-extension 
Privacy policy:

This is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to
Bale.

firefox-addons:3047304.summary: Ten-point OWASP-style security checklist for the page you're on: headers, cookies, mixed content, exposed files, JS library CVEs.
firefox-addons:3047304.description:
A pre-pentest sanity check that takes five seconds instead of fifteen minutes.
Before you pay for a penetration test (or before you ship) there's a set of boring, mechanical misconfigurations that show up on a depressing share of production sites. No HSTS. No CSP. Session cookies without HttpOnly. A .git directory served to the public internet. jQuery 1.8 with four known XSS advisories.
Finding these today means running curl -I, squinting at headers you half-remember, checking DevTools for mixed content, and pasting library versions into a CVE search. That's fifteen minutes per site, so people skip it, so it ships broken.
QuickAudit is that checklist, as one button.
The ten checks:
1. Transport security: HTTPS, plus HSTS with max-age
2. Content-Security-Policy: present, enforcing, and not defeated by 'unsafe-inline' / 'unsafe-eval' / wildcards
3. Clickjacking protection: CSP frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options
4. MIME-sniffing: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
5. Referrer & Permissions policy: flags policies that leak full URLs to third parties
6. Cookie security flags: Secure, HttpOnly on session cookies, explicit SameSite
7. Mixed content: http:// subresources on an HTTPS page
8. JavaScript libraries with known CVEs: versions read from live page globals, looked up against OSV.dev
9. Exposed sensitive files: /.env, /.git/HEAD, etc. (Off by default)
10. Server version disclosure: banners that hand attackers your exact build number
Privacy:
QuickAudit sends exactly one kind of data off your machine: detected library name@version strings, to api.osv.dev, to look up known CVEs. No URLs. No page content. No cookie values: the code reads cookie flags and deliberately discards values. No analytics. No account. No telemetry.
Source: https://github.com/BAB78/quickaudit

firefox-addons:2690100.name: Time Tracker - Web Habit Builder
firefox-addons:2690100.summary: Track time, analyze your habits and block addictive sites
firefox-addons:2690100.description:
Free, open-source screen time tracker, website blocker and focus timer — no account, no ads, no subscription, all data stays local. 🚀
Time Tracker - Web Habit Builder automatically logs every second of your browsing, visualizes digital habits by site, category or tab group, and blocks addictive websites with flexible rules. Built for people who want an honest view of their screen time without handing data to a cloud service.
🌟 CORE CAPABILITIES
⏱ Screen Time Tracking & Audit: High-accuracy engine with active-tab state detection and audible-tab awareness (playing audio/video keeps the clock running). A 3-day rolling granular timeline shows second-by-second activity for deep auditing. Optional idle-pause stops tracking when you step away. Tracks background tabs too via runtimeInfo — a site open in any tab counts, not just the foreground one.
📊 Digital Habit Analysis: Multidimensional reports by Site, Site Category, Tab Group or Merge-site Rules (merge by date / domain / category / tab group). Busyness and Focusness indices surface browsing patterns; habit reports cover Busiest time of day, Longest idle period and Daily trends at 15 min / 30 min / 1 h / 2 h granularity. Media playback time is tracked separately. Fully offline, zero data leakage.
🛡 Website Blocker & Time Limits: Integrated blocker with Daily limit, Weekly limit, Time limit per visit, Blocked periods and focus-session rules. Add Delay count, Locked mode and six unlock verifications (password, custom Q&A, timed typing, 2FA 6-digit code, π digits, confession phrase) to break addictive browsing cycles and protect deep work.
🎯 Focus & Pomodoro: Deep Focus and Pomodoro methods with Allow only / Block filter policies, presets, and pause / extend / end controls — turn any tab set into a distraction-free session.
🔍 Precision "subpage" (Virtual Sites): Beyond domain tracking, define specific sub-page URLs (a YouTube video, a Notion doc, a Gmail label) for granular monitoring. Whitelist sites to skip tracking entirely. Site Category and Merge-site Rules organize long-tail URLs.
🔒 DATA OWNERSHIP AND TRANSPARENCY
🏠 Local-Only Storage: 100% of your history stays on your machine. The extension does not collect, store or transmit browsing data to any remote server.
☁ User-Controlled Sync & Backup: Optional sync across devices via your own GitHub Gist, WebDAV or Obsidian REST accounts. An auto-backup alarm keeps a rolling copy. Connections are authorized and managed entirely by you.
🔐 Data Password (v4.7.0): Lock the dashboard behind a password so nobody browsing over your shoulder can read your history. Unlock to view.
⚖ MIT + Anti-996 Dual License: Transparent, audit-ready source code. No hidden tracking, no subscriptions, no ads.
🔄 SEAMLESS TRANSITION
📥 One-Click Import: Migrate from Webtime Tracker, Web Activity Time Tracker or History Trends Unlimited without losing your history.
📤 Export: Full record export as JSON or CSV, plus site/category export.
💻 Cross-Browser: Native support for Chrome, Firefox (including Firefox for Android) and Edge, with automatic Dark Mode.
→ Source code: https://github.com/sheepzh/time-tracker-4-browser 
→ Report an issue: https://github.com/sheepzh/time-tracker-4-browser/issues 
→ Website: https://time-tracker-4-browser.app

firefox-addons:2805637.name: StayFocused
firefox-addons:2805637.summary: Block distracting websites, track browsing time, and stay productive. Features daily time limits, lockdown mode, focus hour scheduling, in-app "feature" blocking, and Gen AI analytics.
firefox-addons:2805637.description:
StayFocused 
Take control of your browsing habits with powerful, flexible productivity tools.
 Site Blocking 
Block entire domains, subdomains, or specific URL paths (e.g. youtube.com/shorts ). Set a daily time limit — blocked sites are accessible until your budget runs out, then they're locked for the rest of the day.
 Lockdown Mode 
Need to focus right now? Activate Lockdown to block sites for a set duration. Once started, ending early requires completing an extreme typing challenge — no easy way out.
 Focus Hours 
Schedule multiple focus-hour blocks across the week. During active hours, blocked sites are automatically restricted. Visualize your schedule with a weekly calendar heatmap.
 Usage Dashboard 
Track daily browsing with interactive charts :
* Category breakdowns — Social, AI, Entertainment, Productivity, News, Shopping
* Gen AI platform usage — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and more
* Top sites table with per-category labels
* Weekly trends and 7/14/30-day bar charts
 Challenge Protection 
Enable challenge protection to prevent impulsive settings changes. Removing blocked sites, disabling focus hours, or ending lockdown requires typing a long random string manually — no copy-paste allowed.
 Privacy First 
StayFocused only tracks hostnames and time spent. No page content, form data, or personal information is ever collected or transmitted. All usage data stays on your device.
